newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters president to fight US trade legislation.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters president to fight US trade legislation.

text.p: Teamsters President Ron Carey said Tuesday that major trade legislation will be the next battleground for the union now that it has tentatively settled a strike against United Parcel Service.

Carey told a news conference that the union will fight to stop "fast track" trade legislation that would allow U.S. officials to negotiate an expansion of the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) and other trade agreements.

Carey said the two-week strike by 185,000 UPS workers against the nation's largest package delivery service was a battle against a "throw-away workers" approach by corporations. The two sides have reached tentative agreement on a settlement and striking workers are expected to return to their jobs this week.

NAFTA, Carey said, was part of the "same throw-away worker concept. Throw away the jobs of American workers, exploit workers in countries like Mexico for $4 a day and then, if they start to get organized, move from one place to another."

President Clinton is expected to unveil next month proposed fast track legislation that would allow U.S. officials to negotiate trade agreements with other countries without fear they will be later changed by Congress. Lawmakers would be able to vote for or against them, but not amend them.

Labor unions, who view NAFTA as a job loser for American workers, have vowed to fight the proposed fast track legislation. Administration officials, who argue it is needed to open markets to more U.S. exports, have said they hope to have new trade negotiation authority in place by the end of the year.
